notes.type: reference inapplicable to selected edition; original retained
notes.finding: The primary exercise image clearly prints 134. In the selected 1895 second edition of First Book, §134 is munan, not the required strong III system. The Exercises title and preface identify the author’s First Book but do not specify an edition number. No evidence here establishes whether the discrepancy originated in printing or inherited cross-edition references.
notes.correction_for_learner_guidance: Keep 134 in the exact prompt and annotate it as inapplicable to the selected edition. Refer learners to the audited strong III system, Cook §104, and the grammar audit’s directly checked forceorfan lexical entry.
notes.grammar_corroboration: Unit 13 grammar audit independently inspected Cook §134 and the proper strong III system.

notes.finding: The first generated genitive plural mechanically concatenated swētr- and -ra. Personally inspected Wright §259.3, printed 130/PDF 150, requires simplification of doubled r after t; all three gender cells now use swētra. Root independently identified the same defect.

Reading ciricean, ðæcean, unasęcgendre and hwæthwugu remain exact. They are not silently changed to productive model spellings or the exercise’s hwæthwega. Productive nominal paradigms are separate records.
A 600 dpi primary crop settles męte with hooked first e in 24.10 and capital Father in 24.11. Earlier working transcription mete/father is corrected; source itself is not corrected.

The identical source ciricean is genitive at tokens 95, 134 and 183, governed by roof or window, and dative at tokens 16, 28 and 221. Corresponding articles 94, 132 and 182 and ilcan 133 are genitive. Ēode at token 204 is preterite subjunctive in the signal’s purpose or content, whereas token 206 is narrative indicative. Sceolden 175 is preterite subjunctive and hwæt 171 is a predicate nominative. These replace provisional morphological bindings; the exact source spelling is unchanged.

notes.type: explicit interpretation of original pedagogical control
notes.finding: The final parenthetical verb last is interpreted as governing the nearest named verb bebēodan in the relative clause. It does not require the condition’s dōð to follow a subsequent relative. A defensible dōð-final alternative remains valid. The key must distinguish this local control from general tendencies in dependent clauses.

The actual prior productive form wesan-beon-pres-3-sg is bið without a macron, first productive in ch06. Preserve that registered selection. The unmarked bið in Cook’s 24.9 hint is exact source, not a reason to invent a new length-marked productive form.
